related_questions.question: What are the new guidelines for hypertension?
related_questions.snippet: The 2023 ESH guidelines maintain the same BP grade classifications as the 2018 ESC/ESH guidelines. The ESH recommends a threshold of >140/90 mm Hg (grade 1) for the diagnosis of hypertension, whereas the ACC/AHA guideline recommends a lower threshold of >130/80 mm Hg (stage 1).

related_questions.question: What is the CDC classification of hypertension?
related_questions.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) is consistently at or above 130/80 mm Hg. High blood pressure typically has no signs or symptoms but can cause problems for your heart, brain, kidneys, and eyes. No matter your age, you can take steps each day to keep your blood pressure in a healthy range.

related_questions.question: What are the American family physician guidelines for hypertension?
related_questions.snippet: Recommendations and Key Points First, the AAFP recommends that clinicians treat adults with hypertension to a standard blood pressure target of less than 140/90 mm Hg to reduce the risk of all-cause mortality and cardiovascular mortality. This is a strong recommenda- tion based on high-quality evidence.

text_blocks.snippet: The CDC and other health organizations define normal blood pressure as readings below 120/80 mm Hg. Elevated blood pressure is defined as readings between 120/80 and 129/80 mm Hg, and high blood pressure (hypertension) is defined as readings of 130/80 mm Hg or higher.
snippet_highlighted_words: normal blood pressure as readings below 120/80 mm Hg

list.snippet: Elevated: Systolic (top number) between 120-129 and diastolic (bottom number) less than 80.
High (Stage 1): Systolic between 130-139 or diastolic between 80-89.
High (Stage 2): Systolic 140 or higher or diastolic 90 or higher.
Hypertensive Crisis: Systolic higher than 180 or diastolic higher than 120.

text_blocks.snippet: Recommendations for Action Based on Blood Pressure Readings:

list.snippet: Normal: Maintain a healthy lifestyle to prevent high blood pressure.
Elevated: Monitor blood pressure closely and make healthy lifestyle changes.
High (Stage 1): Seek medical advice and discuss lifestyle changes and/or medication.
Hypertensive Crisis: Seek immediate medical attention.

list.title: Accurate Measurement:
list.snippet: Ensure proper technique when measuring blood pressure at home or by a healthcare professional.

list.title: Individualized Approach:
list.snippet: Treatment and management of high blood pressure should be individualized based on factors like age, other medical conditions, and risk factors.

list.title: Lifestyle Modifications:
list.snippet: Healthy lifestyle changes, such as a heart-healthy diet, regular physical activity, weight management, and stress reduction, can significantly impact blood pressure.

list.title: Medication:
list.snippet: For many individuals, medication is necessary to manage hypertension and prevent complications.
